items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Terminology 21:1
items.html: When the upper one couples within himself in order to bring out the lower one, he couples in the externality in him, that is, in a screen that brings out a level lower than his own level. For example, when the upper one is of phase three, he brings out the lower one from a screen of phase two; and if the upper one is of phase two, he brings out the lower one from a screen of phase one, and so forth in this manner. Therefore, when Bina emanates ZA, she does not bring him out from her own level, which is her internality, but from her externality, meaning from a phase lower than her own level. Hence GAR of ZA emerges from the externality of the simple first Hey of SAG, and VAK of ZA emerges from the externality of the two Heys in her filling of Yod. See above, answer 20. Thus ZA emerges from the externality of the three Heys of the first Hey of SAG. (Page 908, Item 71). See answers 3 and 4.
